scope: Reviewed every file in support-agent/: src/*.py, src/tools/*.py, .mcp.json, config/agent.yaml, config/otel-collector.yaml, k8s/deployment.yaml, k8s/networkpolicy.yaml, Dockerfile, requirements.txt, prompts/system.md, CODEOWNERS, README.md. Not found: .brace/deployment.yaml, CI workflows, tests, IaC for IAM, Kubernetes ServiceAccount/RBAC, Redis and Postgres access policies, MCP server source, alerting config, runbooks. Not a git repository, so no commit hash. Code review only; nothing was run.

evidence.note: anthropic_tools() exposes every tool each MCP server lists, with no allowlist filter
stripe MCP server started with --tools=all
policy is a 4-name blocklist; any other tool name is allowed
tool_index filled dynamically from server listings; call() dispatches any listed name
prompt tells the model to call the internal orders API directly, a path outside any tool list

findings.summary: Any tool any of the three MCP servers offers, including all Stripe tools, is callable; there is no allowlist or written inventory.
findings.next_step: Add one explicit per-role allowlist (local + namespaced MCP tools), filter discovered tools against it, reject unknown names in dispatch, drop --tools=all, then run recipe B01.

evidence.note: agent reuses the support rep's OAuth access token for all downstream calls
the rep's bearer token is passed to every MCP server as OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN
tenant_id is a model-filled argument for lookup_order and issue_refund
one DATABASE_URL connection serves all tenants; tenant separation is a WHERE clause on a model-supplied value
one platform-wide STRIPE_SECRET_KEY used for refunds in every tenant

findings.summary: Credentials are inherited from a human and shared across tenants, and the tenant boundary depends on a value the model writes.
findings.next_step: Give the agent its own scoped, audience-bound credentials per tenant; inject tenant_id from the verified run context; then run recipe B02.

evidence.note: INTERNAL_API_KEY read from env and formatted into the system prompt
prompt template contains {internal_api_key}
static API keys and DB URL from a Kubernetes Secret; no expiry or rotation configured
fixed Stripe secret key

findings.summary: A long-lived internal API key is sent to the model in every request, and all credentials are static with no rotation.
findings.next_step: Remove the key from the prompt, move to short-lived workload-identity credentials, add secret scanning and rotation, then run recipe B03.

evidence.note: downstream access uses the launching rep's own OAuth token
every run acts on behalf of the rep via resolve_user_token

findings.summary: Cutting off the agent's Zendesk, Stripe, or Gmail access means revoking the rep's own token, so independent revocation is impossible.
findings.next_step: Issue the agent its own identity and token (token exchange with the rep as delegated subject), set a maximum cutoff time, then run the B04 drill.

evidence.note: only gate before execution is policy.allowed(); no approval step
allowed() is a tool-name blocklist that ignores target and arguments
issue_refund posts a Stripe refund with no approval check
send_email sends to any model-chosen address with no approval
refund limit ($500) exists only as a prompt rule
Stripe MCP with all tools gives a second ungated payment path

findings.summary: Refunds and outbound email run without approval, and the agent reads untrusted tickets, holds customer PII, and sends outside, so every consequential action needs a gate.
findings.next_step: Add an execution-path gate that blocks refunds, email sends, and Stripe/Gmail/Zendesk write tools by default and checks operation, target, and arguments; record the three capabilities; run recipe B05.

evidence.note: no approval record, approver, expiry, or argument binding anywhere in dispatch
decision is a boolean on tool name only

findings.summary: No approval mechanism exists, although B05 requires approvals for refunds and sends.
findings.next_step: Build approvals bound to instance, operation, target, argument hash, approver and expiry, consumed atomically and fail-closed; run recipe B06.

evidence.note: harness enforces step, wall-clock, and token limits per run
per-run tool-call rate limit
per-tenant and fleet daily spend caps in Redis
check_tool_call() raises BudgetExceeded outside the try block, so the rate limit ends the run with an unhandled error and no audit record

findings.summary: Budgets are enforced outside the model, but the tool-rate stop is unhandled and quota checks are read-then-write, so concurrent runs can overshoot.
findings.next_step: Handle the tool-rate stop as an escalation, make quota checks atomic, add timeouts on tool calls, then run recipe B07 including concurrent runs.

evidence.note: egress rule '- {}' allows all egress
privileged container

findings.summary: The pod can reach any network destination, including production and admin systems; no reachable-systems list exists.
findings.next_step: Write the reachable-systems list, replace the allow-all egress with named peers, then run recipe B08.

evidence.note: egress allows everything, including metadata and loopback addresses
prompt directs the model to call an internal API directly

findings.summary: No egress allowlist exists, so leaked data can go to any destination.
findings.next_step: Route egress through a proxy with a destination allowlist, block metadata and direct paths, alert on blocks, then run recipe B09.

evidence.note: image referenced by :latest tag, imagePullPolicy Always
build and push by hand with :latest; no signing or provenance

findings.summary: The image is mutable, unsigned, and has no provenance or admission check.
findings.next_step: Pin by digest, sign and attest in CI, enforce an admission policy in production, then run recipe B10.

evidence.note: privileged: true and runAsUser: 0
final image installs curl, nodejs, npm
no USER line; runs as root
MCP servers downloaded and run with npx -y inside the agent container

findings.summary: The agent runs as a privileged root container with a shell, downloader, and package manager.
findings.next_step: Meet Pod Security 'restricted' (non-root, no escalation, drop ALL, seccomp), use a minimal image, pre-install pinned MCP servers, then run recipe B11.

evidence.note: harness, prompts, config, .mcp.json, and k8s have owners (positive)
production deploy is manual docker push and kubectl apply from a workstation
MCP server code is fetched unpinned at run time, outside review

findings.summary: Reviewed source exists, but deploys happen by hand with no release record linking the running version to a review.
findings.next_step: Deploy only from CI on a protected branch, record the deployed digest against the reviewed commit, pin MCP servers, then run recipe B12.

evidence.note: webhook HMAC verified with compare_digest, body size and schema checked (positive)
signature timestamp is not checked for freshness, so captured webhooks can be replayed
MCP tool output passed to the model with no type, size, or content check
retrieved KB text passed on unchecked
/kb/import accepts content with no authentication

findings.summary: Only the webhook boundary is checked; tool output, retrieved chunks, and KB imports reach the model unvalidated.
findings.next_step: List every input, add size, schema, and content checks with fail-closed handling to tool output and retrieval, authenticate /kb/import, check timestamp freshness, then run recipe R01.

evidence.note: KB articles become context blocks
every tool result is appended to context_blocks
context_blocks are formatted into the system prompt on each call
untrusted context sits inside the system prompt

findings.summary: Untrusted KB text and tool output are placed in the system channel, and no gate contains a followed injection.
findings.next_step: Keep untrusted content in tool-result/user messages with source labels, rely on B01/B02/B05 containment, then run recipe R02 with repeated and adaptive attacks.

evidence.note: internal API key placed in model input
full tool arguments, including email bodies and addresses, written to audit with no redaction
order lookup returns customer email, name, and shipping address to the model
model-written text sent to customers unchecked

findings.summary: A secret and customer PII reach the model and logs with no redaction; SQL is parameterized (src/db.py:10).
findings.next_step: Remove secrets from prompts, redact PII in tool output and audit details, check outbound email content, then run recipe R03 with marker secrets.

evidence.note: /kb/import lets any caller write to the shared index with a self-declared tenant_id
search has no tenant filter on a collection shared by all tenants
chunks lack trust level and time added; no quarantine, expiry, or revoke path

findings.summary: Anyone can poison the shared KB, and one tenant's articles are returned to every other tenant.
findings.next_step: Authenticate and restrict ingestion, add tenant filter in the query, store trust and time metadata, add quarantine/revoke, then run recipe R04.

evidence.note: messages and context are built fresh per run; no memory store or memory-write tool

findings.summary: No memory persists between runs; the KB is a retrieval corpus covered under R04.
findings.next_step: Governance to approve N/A; revisit if any memory or conversation store is added.

evidence.note: no persistent memory; state ends with the run

findings.summary: No memory persists between runs, so memory provenance does not apply.
findings.next_step: Governance to approve N/A.

evidence.note: agent.context.size set from usage.input_tokens and marked 'measured'
value comes from usage.input_tokens, which excludes cache-read and cache-creation tokens
final_answer action carries no context size

findings.summary: Per-action context size is logged, but the counting method is not documented, does not cover cached input or compaction, and is missing on final answers.
findings.next_step: Document the counting method, include cache tokens, record compaction, cover every action, then run recipe R07.

evidence.note: denied tool calls 'continue' with no audit record
telemetry pipeline has no security rules or alert routing

findings.summary: Denied calls are never logged and no security rules or responder routing exist in the repo.
findings.next_step: Emit denials and policy decisions as events, add security rules routed to a named responder, then run recipe R08.

evidence.note: no pre-action checker comparing refunds or emails with the original ticket
denials are not emitted, so repeated-denial sequences can't be detected

findings.summary: The agent can be hijacked through allowed tools, and nothing checks high-impact actions against the original task or detects chains.
findings.next_step: Add a pre-action task-alignment check that doesn't see untrusted content, plus sequence rules split by context size; run recipe R09.

findings.summary: Misaligned-behavior review can't be judged from code, and no threat model states whether misalignment is in scope.
findings.next_step: Record whether misalignment is in scope; if so run recipe R10 with a labeled evasive set and red-team traces.

evidence.note: halt flag is in the same Redis (REDIS_URL) the agent writes for budgets, so the agent's credentials can change it
fails closed when Redis is unreadable (positive)
flag checked only before each model call, not before each tool call or during in-flight tool calls

findings.summary: The stop flag is writable with the agent's own Redis access, and running tool calls are not cancelled.
findings.next_step: Move the stop control to a store the agent can't write, check it before every tool call and cancel in-flight work, name who may stop it, then run the dated R11 drill.

evidence.note: Stripe refund then a separate DB insert, with no transaction, operation record, or reconcile step
halt returns immediately with no handling of queued or in-progress effects
Deployment restarts pods automatically; Zendesk webhook redelivery can restart runs

findings.summary: No per-operation stop plan or reconciliation exists, so a stop mid-refund leaves an unrecorded refund.
findings.next_step: Record per operation whether it can be blocked, cancelled, or reconciled; write operation records before sending; add reconcile steps; run recipe R12.

evidence.note: denials not recorded
tool_call recorded only after success, with no result, no policy version, and no operation ID
audit row has no trace ID, parent link, or result field

findings.summary: A run can't be rebuilt from the audit record: denials, results, errors, and policy versions are missing.
findings.next_step: Record proposed action, decision with policy version, operation ID before sending, result or error, and trace links; then run recipe R13.

evidence.note: Stripe refund sent with no Idempotency-Key
webhook handler has no deduplication by ticket or event ID, so redelivered webhooks rerun the agent

findings.summary: Webhook redelivery can repeat refunds and emails because no idempotency key or duplicate check exists.
findings.next_step: Send Idempotency-Key to Stripe, deduplicate webhook events, pause on unclear results, then run recipe R14.

evidence.note: agent acts with the rep's forwarded OAuth token
a support-agent ServiceAccount exists but downstream calls don't use it

findings.summary: The agent has no identity of its own for Zendesk, Stripe, or Gmail; it acts as the rep.
findings.next_step: Issue an agent principal and exchange tokens with the rep as delegated subject; run recipe A01.

evidence.note: audit rows hold five fields but no trace context
denied actions write no record
a tool exception ends the run with no audit record

findings.summary: Denied and failed actions have no records, and audit rows lack trace context.
findings.next_step: Write all six fields, including trace context, on success, denial, failure, and budget paths; run recipe A02.

evidence.note: container input reads IMAGE_DIGEST from a pod annotation
annotation helpwise.io/image-digest is not set in the pod template, so the container input is constant
model id is the alias claude-3-5-sonnet-latest
MCP server code is unpinned, so the hash doesn't fix tool implementations

findings.summary: The hash method exists, but its container and model inputs aren't fixed, so different builds can share one type ID.
findings.next_step: Feed the real image digest, pin the model snapshot and MCP versions, document the manifest, then run recipe A03.

evidence.note: tenant_id is in the model-filled tool schema
block.input passed straight to local tools; trusted tenant not injected
delegated subject (user_token.subject) not recorded
/kb/import takes tenant_id from the request body

findings.summary: The model chooses the tenant for order lookups and refunds, so one ticket can act on another tenant's orders.
findings.next_step: Remove tenant_id from tool schemas and inject it from the verified run; record the delegated subject; run recipe A04.

evidence.note: owners named (positive)
only containment is one type-wide halt key; no per-instance stop
type ID computed at run time but no stored manifest or registry maps it back

findings.summary: Owners are named, but no manifest registry, runbook, or instance-level containment exists.
findings.next_step: Store manifests keyed by type ID, add per-instance stop, write a lookup runbook, then run the A05 drill.

evidence.note: single loop; no sub-agents, handoffs, or delegated agent tasks

findings.summary: The agent starts no sub-agents.
findings.next_step: Governance to approve N/A.

evidence.note: voyage-3 embedding model used with no recorded version
embedding model not part of the type ID
main model is a moving alias

findings.summary: Helper models aren't listed or recorded with versions.
findings.next_step: List every model call site with a pinned model record and run recipe A07.

evidence.note: model recorded as an alias with no pinned-or-alias label
embedding model absent from any manifest
no release manifest or .brace/ directory in the repo

findings.summary: No release manifest exists.
findings.next_step: Write a manifest covering container digest, harness, prompts, models, tools, MCP servers, scopes, network rules, and budgets; run recipe C01.

evidence.note: review owners for security-relevant paths (positive)
kubectl apply from a workstation bypasses review

findings.summary: Reviews are configured, but production changes bypass them through manual deploys; no emergency-change path is written.
findings.next_step: Deploy only via CI, restrict who can change production config, document emergency changes, then run recipe C02.

evidence.note: :latest image with no digest verification
container input comes from an unset annotation
type ID is never compared with an approved manifest

findings.summary: Nothing checks the running state against an approved manifest, so a changed image or model keeps the same identity.
findings.next_step: Add a startup or admission check against the approved manifest that fails on mismatch; run recipe C03.

evidence.note: npx -y fetches the newest MCP server code at each pod start, outside any baseline
no drift detection config for prompts, MCP lists, or egress

findings.summary: No drift detection exists, and MCP server code drifts by design.
findings.next_step: Add baseline comparisons for images, prompts, MCP lists, and network policy with routed alerts; run the C04 drill.

evidence.note: model alias -latest in production config
MCP packages unpinned
Python dependencies pinned (positive) but with no hashes

findings.summary: Model and MCP server versions change without review.
findings.next_step: Pin a dated model snapshot, log the served version, pin MCP packages, then run recipe C05.

evidence.note: release is a manual build and push; no test or promotion gate
no tests directory or CI workflow present in the repo

findings.summary: No release test suite or gate exists.
findings.next_step: Add a CI suite with allowed tasks and attack cases that blocks promotion; run recipe C06.

evidence.note: each release overwrites :latest, so no previous artifact is kept

findings.summary: There is no retained prior release to roll back to and no rollback procedure.
findings.next_step: Keep digest-pinned prior releases and a written rollback procedure; run the C07 drill.

evidence.note: spans carry agent.type.id (positive)
no retention or archive settings; no manifest store keyed by type ID

findings.summary: Traces can't be linked to a stored manifest, and retention is not configured.
findings.next_step: Archive manifests by type ID with retention matching audit, set trace retention, then run recipe C08.

evidence.note: Zendesk, Stripe, and Gmail MCP servers have no owner mapping
Voyage API, Qdrant, SendGrid, and Google tokeninfo also unmapped

findings.summary: Outside services are used with no responsibility table.
findings.next_step: Write a dependency map and responsibility table with owners on both sides; run recipe E01.

evidence.note: npx -y without versions for all three servers
gmail-mcp-server: unscoped package of unknown publisher

findings.summary: MCP servers are unpinned and unreviewed, including one from an unknown publisher that receives the rep's Gmail token.
findings.next_step: Review publishers, pin versions or digests, scan dependencies; run recipe E02.

evidence.note: tool listings used with no fingerprint comparison

findings.summary: Changed tool descriptions or schemas load without any check.
findings.next_step: Store fingerprints of approved tool metadata and block mismatches; run recipe E03.

evidence.note: tool descriptions passed to the model unchanged with no scan or length limit

findings.summary: Tool metadata reaches the model unscanned.
findings.next_step: Scan and limit all tool metadata, fail closed on scanner error; run recipe E04.

evidence.note: tools keyed by bare name in a flat dict; a later server overwrites an earlier one
local tools shadow MCP tools of the same name with no warning

findings.summary: Tools are not namespaced by server identity, so a server can replace another's tool.
findings.next_step: Key tools by verified server identity plus name and flag duplicates; run recipe E05.

evidence.note: stdio servers launched in the agent container with the rep's token in env
open egress; no gateway between agent and servers

findings.summary: No gateway or sandbox enforces MCP calls.
findings.next_step: Route MCP through an enforced gateway, or sandbox stdio servers with limited files, credentials, and network; run recipe E06.

evidence.note: only inbound channel is the Zendesk webhook; no A2A or peer endpoint

findings.summary: The agent receives no messages from other agents.
findings.next_step: Governance to approve N/A.

evidence.note: no sub-agent or peer-agent delegation in the loop

findings.summary: The agent delegates to no sub-agents or peer agents.
findings.next_step: Governance to approve N/A; MCP tool access is covered by B01/B02.

evidence.note: MCP subprocesses hold the rep's long-lived token, which a stop does not revoke
stop checked only between model calls; in-flight MCP calls not cancelled

findings.summary: Stopping does not reach in-flight tool calls or revoke access held by MCP child processes.
findings.next_step: Propagate cancellation to MCP subprocesses, use short-lived agent credentials revoked on stop; run the E09 drill.

evidence.note: audit written with the same DATABASE_URL the agent's tools use; no append-only enforcement shown
Stripe metadata carries no instance ID, so refunds can't be traced to a run
MCP calls made with the rep's token; no mapping back to agent instance

findings.summary: The agent's own credentials can reach its audit table, and vendor-side actions can't be traced to an instance.
findings.next_step: Write audit to an append-only sink with a separate role, tag vendor calls with instance IDs; run recipe E10.

evidence.note: audit written after the action, so a failed write doesn't stop the action
insecure TLS to Tempo; no retention, integrity, or gap alerts

findings.summary: Audit capture is not fail-closed and has no retention, integrity, or gap detection.
findings.next_step: Set retention (at least six months), integrity checks, delivery alerts, and fail-closed capture for high-impact actions; run recipe E11.

findings.summary: Fleet incident response is drill-based and can't be judged from code; no runbook is in the repo.
findings.next_step: Run the E12 drill and name who decides on outside reporting.
